question: What is the main goal of Emergency Obstetric Care (EmOC)?

options.B: Monitoring normal fetal growth during the third trimester
options.C: Providing routine antenatal counseling and vitamins
options.D: Assessing nutritional status prior to conception

explanation: You've got this! EmOC is all about handling sudden, dangerous emergencies during labor, delivery, and after birth to save both mother and baby. Great job!

question: Why can routine antenatal care alone miss some pregnancy dangers?

options.A: Pregnant women rarely attend clinics during their first trimester
options.B: Antenatal clinics refuse to monitor blood pressure during visits
options.C: Many critical emergencies strike unpredictably without prior warning signs
options.D: Complications only develop after healthcare facilities close for the day

explanation: Even if a pregnancy looks completely healthy, sudden issues like heavy bleeding or high blood pressure can pop up out of nowhere. That is why emergency care is so vital!

question: Which type of facility is fully equipped to perform emergency C-sections?

options.A: Basic Emergency Obstetric Care health posts

explanation: Well done! Major surgeries like Cesarean sections need a CEmOC facility because they have a proper operating theatre and surgical team ready.

question: What is the main difference between BEmOC and CEmOC facilities?

options.A: BEmOC handles medical management and simple procedures without major surgery
options.B: CEmOC facilities never provide newborn resuscitation services
options.C: CEmOC centers only offer outpatient antenatal consultations
options.D: BEmOC facilities routinely perform elective surgical sterilizations

explanation: Think of BEmOC as handling medications, simple births, and first aid, while CEmOC takes on major surgeries and blood transfusions.

question: What symptom turns pre-eclampsia into full-blown eclampsia?

options.A: Total cessation of fetal heart tones
options.B: A sudden drop in body temperature
options.D: Severe localized pain in the lower back

explanation: Spot on! Pre-eclampsia has high blood pressure and protein in the urine, but once seizures start, it is classified as eclampsia.

question: A new mother soaks two heavy pads in twenty minutes and feels dizzy. What should you suspect?
explanation: Rapid, heavy bleeding combined with dizziness is a classic sign of postpartum hemorrhage. Quick action is key here!

question: How many total signal functions define a fully working CEmOC facility?
explanation: You got it! They handle the 7 basic signal functions plus 2 comprehensive ones, bringing the total to 9.

question: Why do health teams check 'signal functions' instead of just looking at hospital buildings?

options.A: To verify that actual life-saving treatments are actively being delivered to patients
options.B: To calculate the exact electricity consumption of hospital lighting
options.C: To determine the architectural layout required for nursing stations
options.D: To audit the daily cleaning schedules of delivery rooms

explanation: A nice building isn't enough! Signal functions prove that the staff, drugs, and equipment are actually there to save lives.

question: What is your very first priority when a pregnant patient arrives in an emergency?

options.A: Completing the hospital billing and admission forms
options.B: Obtaining a detailed family medical history
options.C: Weighing the patient on the clinic scale
options.D: Ensuring a patent airway and stable breathing

explanation: Always remember ABCDE! Airway and breathing come before any paperwork or routine questions in an emergency.

question: Which of these is a dangerous mistake during an emergency obstetric triage?

options.A: Notifying the medical doctor immediately upon finding abnormal bleeding
options.B: Placing an unstable patient in a quiet resuscitation bay
options.C: Delaying vital sign assessment to fill out admission paperwork
options.D: Checking maternal blood pressure upon entry

explanation: Never let paperwork delay patient care! In emergencies, checking vital signs and stabilizing the patient comes first.

question: Which medication is standard for stopping seizures in a pregnant woman with eclampsia?
explanation: Magnesium sulfate is the magic word here! It is the go-to drug to control and prevent seizures in eclampsia.

question: A patient has heavy postpartum bleeding and a soft, boggy uterus. What should you do first?

options.A: Prepare the patient for an immediate MRI scan
options.B: Encourage the patient to walk around the ward
options.D: Insert a nasogastric tube for decompression

explanation: Massaging the uterus helps the muscle contract tightly, which closes off bleeding blood vessels. Great nursing intervention!

question: Why is it important to call the receiving hospital before transferring an emergency patient?

options.A: It allows the receiving team to prepare blood products and surgical staff in advance
options.B: It ensures that the transferring nurse does not need to accompany the patient
options.C: It eliminates the need for any documentation to travel with the patient
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will not incur any hospital treatment fees

explanation: Calling ahead gives the team time to prep the operating room and blood bank so treatment starts the second the ambulance arrives.

question: What must you ensure before sending an emergency obstetric patient on a long ambulance ride?

options.A: The patient has signed discharge papers against medical advice
options.B: All routine hospital laundry duties have been fully completed
options.C: A family member has paid the complete transport fare in cash
options.D: The patient is stabilized and secure intravenous access is established

explanation: Always make sure your patient is as stable as possible with a working IV line so you can give fluids or meds during transit.

question: Why do nurses monitor urine output closely after a patient suffers severe bleeding?

options.A: To calculate the exact dietary protein intake required
options.B: To measure the effectiveness of routine infant feeding schedules
options.C: To evaluate renal perfusion and detect early kidney injury
options.D: To determine when the patient can be discharged home

explanation: When blood loss causes shock, the kidneys can suffer. Watching urine output helps us catch early signs of kidney trouble!

question: What emotional care is essential for a woman recovering from a scary birth emergency?

options.A: Emotional debriefing and supportive counseling about the traumatic event
options.B: Immediate transfer to a psychiatric institution for sedation
options.C: Complete isolation from family members to ensure physical rest
options.D: Strict avoidance of talking about the childbirth experience

explanation: Birth emergencies can be terrifying. A listening ear and compassionate counseling help mothers heal both inside and out.
